explain.say: Tidal stream turbines look like underwater wind turbines standing on the seabed in fast tidal currents. Seawater is about 800 times denser than air, so a cubic metre of moving water is far heavier than a cubic metre of wind.

faq.q: How much denser is water than air?
faq.a: Seawater has a mass of about 1,025 kilograms per cubic metre, while air is only about 1.2 kilograms. That makes seawater roughly 800 times denser.

faq.q: Why does moving water carry so much energy?
faq.a: Kinetic energy depends on mass and speed. A flow of water has hundreds of times more mass than air moving at the same speed, so even a slow current carries a lot of energy.
asks: Is a water current stronger than wind?

faq.q: Where are tidal stream turbines put?
faq.a: In narrow channels where tides rush through fast, such as the Pentland Firth in Scotland, home of the MeyGen project. The turbines sit on the seabed, out of sight and deep enough for ships to pass over.

faq.q: How big are tidal stream turbines?
faq.a: MeyGen's turbines have rotors about 18 metres across and make about 1.5 megawatts each. A wind turbine of the same power needs a rotor roughly four times as wide.
asks: How much power does a tidal turbine make?

faq.q: Do tidal turbines harm sea life?
faq.a: The blades turn fairly slowly, and monitoring so far suggests seals and fish mostly avoid them, but scientists keep watching. Noise and effects on the seabed are also studied before turbines go in.
asks: Are tidal turbines safe for fish?

facts: Seawater is about 800 times denser than air.
The MeyGen tidal stream project in Scotland's Pentland Firth first sent power to the grid in 2016.
